name: InfiniteMemory Agent
description: Instructions for InfiniteMemoryAgent: the root, generator, and verifier rules that each agent's system prompt carries, the messages that brief a generator, a verifier, and a resumed root, the result card a parent receives for each pair, the replies of the memory tools and their quota line, the workspace map's header, and the model-facing descriptions of launch_subagent, remember, write_note, edit_file, and drop_entry and of their parameters.

prompts.replayed_label: (Replayed: this pair already finished earlier in this run, so it was not run again.)
prompts.launch_rejected_prompt: No task was started, because the batch needs a change: {problem} Fix the tasks and call launch_subagent again.
prompts.memory_rejected_prompt: Nothing was saved, because the call needs a change: {problem} Fix it and call the tool again, or move on.
prompts.remember_staged_prompt: Staged as {key}. It is saved to memory only after the verifier has checked this pair's work.
prompts.entry_dropped_prompt: Dropped {key}, so it will not be saved. Staged entries still waiting for the verdict: {remaining}.
prompts.quota_line: Quota left: {entries_left} of {entries_max} memory entries and {files_left} of {files_max} new files.
prompts.map_header: Files: {files} of {max_files}. Tokens: {tokens} of {max_tokens}. Live memory entries: {entries}. Each line below is one workspace file with its token count and description.
prompts.launch_tasks_description: The tasks to run, from 1 to {max_parallel}, each with a name that is unique in this call. Write each task for agents that cannot see this conversation.
prompts.launch_name_description: A short lowercase name for the task: letters, digits, and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit, at most 40 characters. It names the pair in its result card and must be unique in this call.
prompts.launch_goal_description: What the task must achieve, in one or two sentences.
prompts.launch_done_criteria_description: At least one checkable condition that is true when the task is done. The verifier checks the work against each one.
prompts.launch_generator_prompt_description: Complete instructions for the generator, the agent that does the work. It cannot see this conversation, so say everything it needs.
prompts.launch_verifier_prompt_description: Instructions for the verifier, the agent that checks the generator's work after it finishes: what to check and how. It sees the goal, the done criteria, the generator's summary, its staged memories, and the files it wrote.
prompts.launch_context_description: Memory entry ids such as #12 and workspace file paths the pair should start from. Entries are pasted into the generator's first message, and files are listed by path for it to read.
prompts.launch_tools_description: Names of extra tools the pair needs, chosen from the extra tools you hold yourself. Leave it out when the preset tools are enough.
prompts.remember_tool_description: Save one short memory entry that later agents in this run, and later runs, can find. Use it only for what will matter again: a decision, a fact, a lesson, an open question, or a pointer to a file. The text must be one short line, and the same text cannot be saved twice. Each agent has a small quota of entries, shown after every call. In a pair, entries are staged and saved only after the verifier has checked the work; to replace an outdated entry, give its id in supersedes.
prompts.remember_kind_description: What the entry records: decision, fact, lesson, open_question, or pointer.
prompts.remember_text_description: The entry itself, as one short line that makes sense on its own.
prompts.remember_tags_description: Up to three lowercase tags of letters, digits, and hyphens that help later searches.
prompts.remember_refs_description: Up to three references of one line each, such as workspace file paths or source URLs.
prompts.remember_supersedes_description: The id of a saved entry that this one replaces; the old entry moves out of the live memory.
prompts.write_note_tool_description: Write longer material to a file in the shared workspace, where every agent and later runs can read it. Give a path inside the workspace that ends in .md, .txt, .json, or .jsonl; seed files, run journals, and the three memory files cannot be written. A new file needs a one-line description for the workspace map, and each agent may create only one new file. Writing to an existing file appends the text to its end. Every file and the workspace as a whole have size limits, and a write over a limit is refused.
prompts.note_path_description: The file's path relative to the workspace folder, such as notes/pricing.md.
prompts.write_note_text_description: The text to write. For an existing file it is appended to the end.
prompts.write_note_file_description: A one-line description of a new file for the workspace map. It is required when the file does not exist yet and ignored otherwise.
prompts.edit_file_tool_description: Replace one passage of an existing workspace file with new text. The old text must appear exactly once in the file, so include enough of it to be unique. Seed files, run journals, and the three memory files cannot be edited. The file and workspace size limits still apply after the change. Use it to correct a file in place instead of appending a correction.
prompts.edit_file_old_text_description: The exact text to replace. It must appear exactly once in the file.
prompts.edit_file_new_text_description: The text that takes its place.
prompts.drop_entry_tool_description: Drop one memory entry that the generator or you staged, so that it is never saved. Name it by its staged key, such as s2, as listed in your first message or in the result of remember. Drop entries that are wrong, duplicated, or not worth keeping, and add a corrected one with remember when it still matters. The entries you do not drop are saved after your final reply when it carries a verdict. The result lists the staged keys that remain.
prompts.drop_entry_id_description: The staged key of the entry to drop, such as s2.
